The search found no mix that meets the full job criteria. I’ll check published analogue mixes to put the two returned candidates in context, since the rheology models have wide uncertainty.
**No mix in the default OPC-required 3DCP search met this wall’s buildability criteria.** The engine screened 4,096 mixes and found none feasible for the 600 mm wall at the specified speed and 60-minute open time.

Its highest-ranked buildability candidate is **100% Portland cement, w/b 0.335, s/b 2.93**. The calculator still rates it **non-printable**, predicting plastic collapse at layer **7 of 48** and free-wall buckling at layer **12**. Its estimated initial static yield stress is **630 [22, 10,908] Pa (q50 [q10, q90])**. That very wide interval makes the rheology estimate order-of-magnitude guidance.

Published mixes provide stronger rheology evidence for a trial formulation. For example, the 3DCP mortar **SP20-HPMC07-PE1.5** (DOI: 10.1016/j.cemconcomp.2024.105599) reports measured static yield stress of **3.81 kPa** and Athix of **15.4 Pa/s**. Its reported composition is OPC/fly ash/silica fume **0.50/0.40/0.10**, w/b **0.26**, s/b **0.20**, PCE **0.20%**, VMA **0.07%**, and fibre **1.50 vol%**. These measurements make it a useful experimental analogue, but they do not establish buildability for your unbraced wall.

The search used the calculator’s defaults of **12.5 mm layer height**, **29.61 mm layer width**, **60 s layer cycle**, and **1.5 safety factor**. The next design step is to change the wall support or geometry and rerun the search; any candidate then needs a print trial.

input.title: Buildability assessment and default 3DCP mix design
input.markdown:
# Buildability assessment and mix-design search

## Job and assumptions
Straight, unbraced wall: target height 600 mm; length 1,500 mm; two filaments; 25 mm nozzle; print speed 50 mm/s; open time 60 min. Calculator defaults: layer height 12.5 mm, layer width 29.61 mm, 48 layers, 60 s layer cycle, density 2,100 kg/m³, elastic-modulus-to-yield-stress ratio 25, and safety factor 1.5.

## Assessment of supplied material
Measured initial static yield stress 3,000 Pa and Athix 1 Pa/s. Physical verdict: **non-printable**. Free-wall buckling governs at layer 17 (about 213 mm); plastic collapse is also expected before the 600 mm target. The 48 min print fits within the 60 min open time. At the current cycle time, avoiding plastic collapse alone would require approximately 7,825 Pa initial static yield stress or 2.675 Pa/s Athix, holding the other property fixed. These thresholds do not clear the buckling check.

## Default 3DCP inverse design, OPC required
The engine sampled 4,096 mixes and found **no feasible mix** for this job. Its leading buildability candidate is Portland cement 1.00, w/b 0.335, s/b 2.93. It is **non-printable**: predicted plastic collapse at layer 7 and buckling at layer 12, against 48 required layers. Predicted initial static yield stress is q50 [q10, q90] = 630 [22, 10,908] Pa. Rheology predictions are order-of-magnitude guidance because the model interval is wide.

A published 3DCP rheology analogue, SP20-HPMC07-PE1.5 (DOI 10.1016/j.cemconcomp.2024.105599), reports measured static yield stress 3.81 kPa and Athix 15.4 Pa/s. Its composition is OPC/fly ash/silica fume 0.50/0.40/0.10, w/b 0.26, s/b 0.20, PCE 0.20%, VMA 0.07%, and fibre 1.50 vol%. This is evidence for a trial formulation, not verification of this wall.

## Recommendation
Revise wall support or geometry and rerun buildability and design. Verify rheology, extrusion, and the full-height print experimentally before adopting a mix.
